finding.claim: Shares cannot be revoked: access granted via /n/<nid>/share is append-only, so a previously shared user keeps read access indefinitely and the owner has no way to withdraw it (MEDIUM, logic gap).
finding.source: Authenticated prior collaborator (a user the owner once shared with), reading GET /n/<nid>.

trace.note: require_edit restricts sharing to the owner
n["shared"].append(request.json["user"]) - grants are only ever added
can_view returns True for any user in note["shared"]
read() calls require_view on every GET
full note returned to the still-shared user

finding.guards_checked: require_edit on share (owner-only sharing); shared users cannot write (can_edit is owner-only) or re-share; abort(403) on failed checks. No removal/unshare path exists anywhere in notes.py, so no control revokes the grant.

verdict.guard_found: require_edit at notes.py:44 restricts sharing to the owner (can_edit at notes.py:17); require_view at notes.py:28 enforces can_view (notes.py:8). No unshare/revoke route exists in notes.py (the only file in the directory), so there is no removal path.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code (notes.py:8, 28-29, 41-45), but the reader's access comes from an owner-authorized grant at notes.py:45 and the code grants them no power beyond what can_view allows (notes.py:8), so this is a missing revocation feature rather than an authorization bypass; the candidate's own attacker is a user the owner deliberately shared with. It may be worth raising as a design gap, but it does not meet the bar for a reachable vulnerability.

finding.claim: Share target is unvalidated and duplicates accumulate: request.json['user'] is stored without type, existence, or duplicate checks, and the list grows without bound, making every can_view scan O(n) (LOW; self-affecting unless usernames can be re-registered, which depends on an identity system outside this repository).
finding.source: Note owner submitting a POST body to /n/<nid>/share.
finding.sink: Append into n['shared'] (notes.py:45), later scanned by can_view (notes.py:8).

trace.note: require_edit: only the owner reaches this line
request.json['user'] appended with no validation or dedupe
user in note['shared'] linear scan on every read/share check

finding.guards_checked: require_edit (owner-only). No validation of value type, account existence, duplicates, or list length.

verdict.guard_found: require_edit (notes.py:20-22) calls can_edit (notes.py:16-17, owner == user) and abort(403) on failure, so only the owner reaches notes.py:45. No validation of type, account existence, duplicates, or list length exists anywhere in notes.py.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code (notes.py:44-45 and 8), but the only actor who can reach the append at notes.py:45 is the note owner (require_edit, notes.py:20-22 aborts with 403 otherwise), and that owner can already add any user to the share list, so the unbounded or duplicate growth only degrades the owner's own note and grants no new privilege; the cross-user case depends on username re-registration in an external identity system that this repository does not contain.

finding.claim: Full collaborator list disclosed to every viewer: jsonify(n) returns owner and shared fields to any user passing can_view, so a shared recipient can enumerate all other collaborators (LOW, non-actionable on its own).
finding.source: Any authenticated user passing can_view (owner or shared recipient) requesting GET /n/<nid>.
finding.sink: Response body via jsonify(n) at notes.py:29.

trace.note: require_view passes for a shared user
jsonify(n) serializes the whole note, including the shared list

finding.guards_checked: require_view / can_view gates access to the note, but the response is not filtered by role, so shared viewers see the owner and full shared list.

verdict.guard_found: require_view (notes.py:11-13) gates access by calling can_view (notes.py:7-8) and aborting with 403 on failure, and the call at notes.py:28 is a bare statement whose abort is effective. Nothing filters the fields in the response: jsonify(n) at notes.py:29 serializes the full note dict, including owner and shared.
verdict.reason: All trace lines are accurate (route at notes.py:26, require_view at notes.py:28, jsonify(n) at notes.py:29 returns the whole note), and a shared user passes can_view (notes.py:8), so the owner and full shared list are disclosed to them with no field filtering. Severity is low: the attacker is an authenticated user who already has view access to the note, and the disclosed data is collaborator metadata rather than note content or a privilege it could not otherwise use.

finding.claim: Unknown note IDs return HTTP 500 (KeyError) while existing-but-forbidden notes return 403, creating an existence oracle for note IDs (LOW; exploitable only if IDs are guessable, and the ID scheme is not in this file).
finding.source: Any caller of GET/PUT/POST on /n/<nid> with an arbitrary nid.
finding.sink: Dict lookup NOTES[nid] at notes.py:27, 34, 43 vs abort(403) at notes.py:13, 22, 36.

trace.note: n = NOTES[nid] raises KeyError for unknown nid, yielding 500
require_view abort(403) for existing notes the caller cannot read
write() has the same KeyError-before-check behavior
share() has the same KeyError-before-check behavior

finding.guards_checked: Authorization checks run after the lookup, so the 500 path bypasses any 403 handling. No 404 handling, no uniform error response.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only checks are require_view/require_edit/can_edit at notes.py:13, 22, 36, and each runs after the unguarded dict lookup at notes.py:27, 34, 43, so nothing prevents the KeyError. No try/except, 404 handler, or uniform error response exists in notes.py.
verdict.reason: notes.py:27 (and 34, 43) index NOTES[nid] before any authorization check, so an unknown nid raises KeyError and returns 500, while an existing note the caller cannot access hits abort(403) at notes.py:13/22/36, giving an existence oracle; the route is reachable by any caller, and severity stays LOW because it only matters if note IDs are guessable. Caveat: g.user is never set in this file, so the 403-vs-500 split for existing notes depends on middleware outside notes.py that sets g.user.
